idiom_name: abstract base class (default interface members for stateless layers)
implementation_notes: C# declares the layer's type with an abstract class: implemented members carry the shared state and behavior, abstract members are the layer's requirements, and the compiler refuses instantiation and incomplete subclasses; a protected constructor establishes the shared state and sealed members freeze invariants. Since C# 8 an interface may also carry default implementations, so a stateless layer contract can be shared without consuming the single class slot - but interface defaults are reached only through the interface and are not inherited as class members. Frameworks ship the layer supertype ready-made (ASP.NET Core's ControllerBase, EF Core's DbContext), and inheriting from those beats rebuilding their surface.
pitfalls: Calling an overridable member from a base constructor dispatches to the derived override before its fields are initialised.

Default interface members are not inherited by classes and cannot be called on a class reference unless the member is redeclared, so mixing abstract classes and interface defaults in one layer makes dispatch hard to follow.
Protected mutable state in the base is part of every subclass's contract and cannot be tightened later without breaking the layer (fragile base class).
